name: Copy and Paste in Text Boxes
description: Lets you copy and paste in the game's text boxes (the tribe name when a new village starts and the villager names on the Details screen, and every other box you type in). While a box has typing focus: Ctrl+V or Shift+Insert pastes the text on the Windows clipboard where you type (the boxes have no movable caret, so at the end of the text); Ctrl+C or Ctrl+Insert copies the box's whole text; Ctrl+X cuts it (copies it, then empties the box). Pasted text keeps the box's own rules: its own character filter (a numbers-only box takes only digits), and its own length limit, cut before the first character that does not fit, never inside a character. Line breaks and tabs become spaces; other control characters are dropped, and so is every character the game cannot show (never turned into '?'): **with Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts or Use Unicode Font on, every character those patches let you type is pasted (at least every Windows-1252 character: accented letters, curly quotes, €, ...); with neither, plain English letters, digits and signs only.** The keys never reach the game as letters or shortcuts. Ctrl+A does nothing: the game's boxes have no selection. When the clipboard is busy or holds no text, nothing happens. **On by default.** **Needs no other patch; works with or without Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts and Use Unicode Font.** **Not yet seen in a running game** (checked by emulation of each stock executable). The companion is "VVFP Copy and Paste.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; saves are never written by it.
behavior_changes: The event pump's SDL_KEYDOWN case (0x4048A6) first asks the companion about the key: Ctrl+V, Shift+Insert, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Insert and Ctrl+X (no Alt, no Windows key), while a text box has typing focus, are handled and the pump goes on with the next event; every other key, and these keys while no box has focus, go on to the stock case exactly as before.

The focused box is found the way the game types into it: the game's own keyboard listeners (event manager 0x4CB508), in the game's order, the first whose keyboard handler is the text box's (0x40D750) that has focus ([box+0x25]) on a screen that takes input.

Paste: the clipboard's CF_UNICODETEXT, composed (NFC) and split into whole characters, CR/LF/Tab as spaces, other control characters and lone surrogates dropped, each character turned into the box's bytes (UTF-8 when the loaded Unicode companion -- VVFP Unicode Text.dll, else VVFP Unicode Font.dll -- answers VvfpGlyphsUtf8() == 1; every printable Windows-1252 character when it answers 0; printable ASCII when neither is loaded), a character the game cannot show dropped, a numbers-only box's filter applied, and the whole cut before the first character that does not fit the box's byte limit ([box+0x28]). UTF-8 text goes in through that companion's VvfpBoxInsertUtf8 (it inserts as typing does); otherwise the bytes are typed into the box through its own handler, one character message each.
Copy: the box's text bytes, read back by the same rule, put on the clipboard as CF_UNICODETEXT; Cut: the same, then (only when the copy succeeded) the box's own Backspace for each byte.
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion replaces the SDL_KEYDOWN case's first ten bytes at run time, only after verifying their stock bytes, and installs nothing on a different build.

Nothing is written but a focused box's text, through the box's own handler and its own rules: opening and closing a box without these keys leaves its bytes exactly as they were. Saves, villager records and the patcher's files are never written.
The clipboard is opened and closed on the game thread and never waited for; busy or empty means nothing happens. A fault is abandoned and the key goes on to the stock code.
The SDL_TEXTINPUT case (detoured by Render Unicode with In-Game Fonts) is not touched; both patches work together or alone.

runtime_detours.routine: the event pump's SDL_KEYDOWN case (mov ecx, [esp + sym]; cmp ecx, imm32)
runtime_detours.installed_by: VVFP Copy and Paste.dll, VvfpStartup (started by VVFP Startup.dll, second word)
